title: Expiry Reminder Standard and Relock Fee Multiplier — Builder Extended Rate Lock
content:
The expiry reminder on a Builder Extended Rate Lock is part of the lock's servicing record, and the notice it gave scales the relock fee when an expired lock is relocked.

**Rule.** The reminder lead is the calendar days from the latest expiry reminder on the lock ledger to the expired lock's expiration date. Where the ledger carries no expiry reminder, the floored relock fee is multiplied by 0.4. Where the reminder lead is shorter than the term's expiry reminder days, the floored relock fee is multiplied by 0.5 plus the reminder lead divided by twice the term's expiry reminder days, so the multiplier grows with the notice actually given. Where the reminder lead is the term's expiry reminder days or longer, the floored relock fee is charged as figured, the multiplier being one. The multiplied amount is rounded half up to the cent.

The floored relock fee is the relock fee after its minimum has been applied.

## Expiry reminder days by term

| Lock term | Expiry reminder days |
|---|---|
| 60-Day Standard Lock | 10 |
| 90-Day Lock | 10 |
| 120-Day Extended Lock | 10 |
| 180-Day Extended Lock | 15 |
| 270-Day Build Lock | 15 |
| 360-Day Build Lock | 15 |

## Method by ledger record

| Lock ledger | Multiplier on the floored relock fee |
|---|---|
| no expiry reminder | 0.4 |
| latest expiry reminder with a lead shorter than the term's expiry reminder days | 0.5 plus the lead divided by twice the term's expiry reminder days |
| latest expiry reminder with a lead equal to or longer than the term's expiry reminder days | one |

## Worked cases (hypothetical inputs)

- A 180-Day Extended Lock, floored relock fee USD 1443.75, latest reminder 6 days before the expiration date: 0.5 plus 6 divided by 30 gives 0.7; 1443.75 multiplied by 0.7 is 1010.625, rounded half up USD 1010.63.
- The same lock with no expiry reminder on its ledger: 1443.75 multiplied by 0.4 is USD 577.50.
- A 90-Day Lock whose latest reminder came exactly 10 days before the expiration date: the multiplier is one and the floored fee stands.
